company_name: Southern Cross Media Group Limited (Southern Cross Austereo)
overview: Southern Cross Media Group (SCA, trading as SXL on the ASX) is an Australian media company built on the Triple M and Hit radio networks (104+ stations) and the LiSTNR digital audio platform. Having fully exited regional television in FY2025 (licences sold to Network Ten and Seven West Media), the company reversed course and acquired 100% of Seven West Media Limited (SWM) -- owner of the Seven Network free-to-air TV business, 7plus streaming, The West Australian newspaper, Pacific Magazines and The Nightly -- in a scrip deal that completed 7 January 2026 (consolidated from 23-24 December 2025). SXL is now an integrated television, audio and publishing business operating solely within Australia, monetised almost entirely through advertising.

business_model.summary: Revenue is earned by selling advertising inventory across free-to-air television (Seven Network and its regional affiliates), broadcast radio (Triple M, Hit, national sales representation of partner regional stations), digital audio (LiSTNR app, podcasts, streaming), and publishing/digital (7plus BVOD, The West Australian, Pacific Magazines, The Nightly). Revenue is advertising-driven, transactional and cyclical rather than subscription-based; multi-year sports broadcast rights (AFL, Cricket Australia, Commonwealth Games, NFL, Rugby League World Cup) anchor ratings and audience reach but represent large, largely fixed content costs. FY2026 (year to 30 June 2026, first year including SWM from late December 2025) group gross revenue was approximately A$1.87 billion, down ~4.5% on the prior year as a soft TV advertising market offset share gains and digital growth.

revenue_streams.name: Broadcast Radio (Triple M, Hit, national representation)
Publishing & other digital (The West Australian, Pacific Magazines, The Nightly)

business_model.customer_type: B2B -- advertisers and media agencies buying national, metro and regional advertising campaigns; audiences/listeners/viewers are free, ad-supported
business_model.geographic_mix: 100% Australia; no material international or currency exposure

main_competitors: News Corp Australia / Foxtel Media (Kayo, Binge)
Global digital platforms (Google, Meta, TikTok, Spotify) competing for ad dollars
competitive_position.market_position: Leading regional and metro radio network (36.7% share of the critical 25-54 metro audience in FY25, #1 network for 32+ consecutive ratings surveys; ~70% of regional radio listening). Seven Network holds a record ~44% share of the metro free-to-air TV market (H1 FY26) on the back of AFL, cricket, Commonwealth Games and NFL rights, but the overall FTA TV ad pool is shrinking. LiSTNR is described by management as Australia's leading digital audio platform with 2.4m+ signed-in users.

moat_factors.description: Spectrum-licensed free-to-air TV and radio licences limit new entrants, though content and audience attention increasingly migrate to unlicensed digital platforms

Long-term AFL (~A$4.5bn over 7 years to 2031), Cricket Australia, Commonwealth Games (Glasgow 2026/2030) and NFL rights drive ratings and advertiser demand, but are expensive and reports suggest Seven has sought to renegotiate the AFL deal
Triple M/Hit dominance in the 25-54 demographic and Seven's record FTA share give scale advantages in media buying, but audience share is contested survey-to-survey (e.g. ARN's Nova gains)
Post-merger, SXL can offer national advertisers a single buy across TV, radio, digital audio and publishing -- a reach advantage over single-medium rivals, though cross-sell synergies are unproven
LiSTNR's 2.4m+ signed-in users and AdTech Hub support targeted, addressable audio advertising, a differentiator versus traditional broadcast-only radio

weaknesses: No recurring/subscription revenue base -- entirely dependent on cyclical advertising spend
Free-to-air TV advertising is in structural decline (metro market down ~9.9% in FY2026) with no clear catalyst for reversal
High fixed content costs from sports rights that are difficult to exit or renegotiate quickly
Leverage increased materially from consolidating SWM's debt onto the balance sheet
Severe post-merger leadership instability undermines execution credibility

growth_drivers: LiSTNR digital audio scaling profitably (34% revenue CAGR since FY20, EBITDA cash-flow positive, AdTech Hub lifting average booking value 79% YoY) in a category management says is structurally under-monetised (34% of consumer media time vs only 8% of ad spend)

Cost synergies from the SWM merger: A$30m of annualised merger synergies delivered ahead of the original 18-24 month schedule, within a broader program now targeting A$145-150m of annualised savings (including ~250-300 FTE job cuts)
Cross-selling advertising packages across TV, radio, digital audio and publishing to national advertisers ("one-stop shop")

7plus BVOD and digital publishing (The Nightly) growth -- group digital revenue (7plus + LiSTNR + The Nightly) rose 11% to A$320m in FY2026, outpacing the decline in linear/broadcast revenue for the first time
Marquee sports and events content (AFL, Cricket Australia, Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games, Rugby League World Cup 2026, NFL) driving ratings and advertiser demand
Debt refinanced into a single A$569m facility with first maturities pushed out to FY2030, reducing near-term refinancing risk and buying time for the turnaround
Contingent 32.5% profit-share consideration from the Network Ten regional TV sale (though the estimated value has already been written down sharply as the regional TV market deteriorated)

business.risk: Structural decline in free-to-air TV and traditional radio advertising
business.description: Metro FTA TV ad market contracted ~9.9% in FY2026 with conditions worsening in Q4; ad dollars continue migrating to digital/social platforms
Two large, culturally distinct businesses (audio-digital SCA and legacy TV/publishing SWM) must be merged while simultaneously cutting ~250-300 jobs and chasing A$145-150m of synergies
AFL rights alone are reported at ~A$4.5bn over 7 years (2025-2031); media reports suggest Seven has sought to renegotiate the deal, implying cash strain
ARN Media/Nova contesting radio audience share, Nine and Network Ten in TV, and global platforms (Google, Meta, TikTok, Spotify) taking a growing share of total ad spend

business.risk: Contingent liabilities from the TV divestment
business.description: Potential termination fee of up to A$23.8m under the amended BAI transmission services agreement, and the NPV of the Network Ten profit-share receivable has already been cut from A$12.7m to A$3.0m as the regional TV market weakened

financial.description: SWM's debt was consolidated onto the balance sheet; pre-merger screen metrics already showed stretched coverage (D/E ~2.2x, net debt/EBITDA ~3.9x, interest coverage ~1.5x), and total borrowings rose to over A$420m at 31 Dec 2025 versus A$67.6m net debt at FY2025
A$11.3m of SWM transaction costs and further restructuring charges (~A$20m in FY2026) are depressing statutory earnings during the integration period
No interim FY2026 dividend was declared and the dividend reinvestment plan has been suspended, reducing near-term shareholder returns

regulatory.description: The ACCC and ACMA cleared the SWM acquisition subject to undertakings; commentary has suggested the deal's timing let it avoid Australia's revised merger-review regime, inviting future regulatory or political scrutiny
Australian media ownership rules, local content quotas and spectrum licence conditions constrain strategic flexibility

macro.description: Revenue is almost entirely transactional advertising spend, highly correlated with consumer and business confidence and GDP growth
Higher leverage post-merger increases sensitivity of earnings and covenant headroom to interest rate movements
Structural shift of advertising budgets from broadcast TV/radio to global digital platforms is a long-run headwind independent of the economic cycle

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Australian free-to-air TV advertising is in structural decline (metro market down ~9.9% in FY2026); broadcast radio is roughly stable to slightly growing; digital audio and BVOD/streaming are the fastest-growing categories and are offsetting some of the linear decline. Audio remains under-monetised relative to listening share, a potential long-term tailwind for LiSTNR specifically.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High -- advertising revenue is discretionary and closely tracks consumer and business confidence and the broader economic cycle
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate-to-high following the debt-funded (via SWM balance-sheet consolidation) increase in leverage; the company refinanced into a single A$569m facility with maturities from FY2030
key_input_costs: Sports broadcast rights (AFL, Cricket Australia, Commonwealth Games, NFL, Rugby League World Cup)

recent_developments.event: FY2025 results: completed full exit from regional television (sale of 3-aggregated-market licences to Network Ten in March 2025, remaining regional TV assets to Seven West Media in June 2025); underlying EBITDA from continuing (audio) operations rose 34% to A$71.1m and a fully franked 4cps final dividend was reinstated
Southern Cross Media Group and Seven West Media announced a proposed scrip merger valued at over A$400m
SWM consolidated into SCA's accounts, reflecting the date of effective control ahead of legal completion

Merger formally completed: SCA acquired 100% of SWM, issuing 238.9m shares (A$189.9m) to SWM holders; SWM delisted; combined group trades as SXL with legacy SCA holders ~50.1% and legacy SWM holders ~49.9%

H1 FY2026 results (6 months to 31 Dec 2025): revenue A$254.7m (+21.5%, including 8 days of SWM); EBITDA excluding SWM and significant items A$40.1m (+28.5%); statutory loss of A$7.4m driven by an A$9.6m loss from discontinued TV operations (write-down of the Network Ten profit-share receivable) and A$11.3m of SWM transaction costs; no interim dividend declared

Leadership turmoil: Chairman Kerry Stokes stepped down (Heith Mackay-Cruise, ex-SCA chair, took over); CEO Jeff Howard departed effective immediately only weeks into the merged role; John Kelly (former SCA CEO) named interim CEO for TV and radio while a global search for a permanent CEO began

Announced 250-300 job cuts and a ~A$20m restructuring charge; cut FY2026 guidance (revenue ~2.5% below prior guidance of A$1.91-1.92bn; underlying EBITDA guidance lowered to A$185-190m) as the advertising market, particularly TV, deteriorated sharply in Q4

FY2026 full-year results: gross revenue ~A$1.87bn (-4.5%); EBITDA A$200m including onerous contracts / A$191.9m excluding (beating the revised guidance); NPAT A$9.9m; digital revenue (7plus + LiSTNR + The Nightly) up 11% to A$320m; A$30m of merger synergies delivered ahead of schedule; broader synergy target raised to A$145-150m annualised; debt refinanced into a single A$569m facility with maturities pushed to FY2030; no explicit FY2027 revenue/EBITDA guidance given, only qualitative caution on advertising conditions

Analyst actions since the merger closed: UBS maintained Hold, cutting its target to A$0.62 (May 2026); Ord Minnett reinstated coverage with a Buy and A$0.75 target (March 2026); Canaccord Genuity had a pre-merger Buy at A$1.08 (October 2025, now likely stale). Shares traded around A$0.48-0.54 in late 2026, implying a market capitalisation of roughly A$230-260m

items.notes: Original guidance was A$1.91-1.92bn; cut ~2.5% in June 2026 due to a deteriorating TV advertising market, then reported in line with the revised figure

items.target: A$185-190m (ex onerous contracts) guided; A$191.9m actual
items.notes: Original FY2026 guidance was A$200-220m; cut in June 2026 amid soft Q4 TV advertising, then actual results came in slightly above the revised range

items.target: A$145-150 million annualised run-rate (including A$30m of merger synergies already delivered)
items.notes: Original merger synergy target was A$25-30m over 18-24 months; A$30m was delivered ahead of schedule and the target was broadened/raised to A$145-150m via a wider cost-out program including 250-300 job cuts
No explicit dollar guidance; management flagged continued cost discipline

Management described advertising conditions as 'subdued and volatile'; early Q1 FY2027 trading showed TV revenue flat YoY, audio up low single digits, and publishing stable, aided by major sporting events

guidance.management_commentary: Management has repeatedly cut and then narrowly beaten revised guidance through FY2026 as the TV advertising market deteriorated faster than expected, while emphasising that digital revenue (7plus/LiSTNR/The Nightly) grew faster than the decline in linear revenue for the first time. The FY2026 result was framed as a 'strategic reset' focused on content, advertiser relationships and financial discipline, with cost synergies delivered ahead of schedule but no firm quantitative outlook given for FY2027 beyond qualitative caution on ad market conditions.

bull_case: LiSTNR is a genuine, profitable growth asset in a structurally under-monetised category (audio is 34% of consumer media time but only 8% of ad spend), diversifying SXL away from pure linear TV/radio decline
The combined TV + radio + digital audio + publishing footprint gives advertisers a unique national one-stop-shop, a scale advantage no single-medium competitor can match

A$30m of merger synergies were delivered ahead of schedule, and a credible, broadened A$145-150m annualised cost-out program offers a meaningful earnings lever even if the advertising market stays weak

Several brokers reinstated or maintained Buy ratings post-merger (Ord Minnett A$0.75, Canaccord A$1.08 pre-merger) against a share price trading around A$0.48-0.54, implying significant perceived upside if execution improves
Debt refinanced into a single A$569m facility with maturities pushed out to FY2030 removes near-term refinancing risk and buys management time to execute the turnaround
bear_case: Free-to-air TV advertising is in structural decline (metro market -9.9% in FY2026) with no clear catalyst for a reversal, and TV is now the company's largest revenue segment post-merger

Leverage increased materially from consolidating SWM's debt; pre-merger coverage metrics were already thin (interest coverage ~1.5x, net debt/EBITDA ~3.9x), leaving limited buffer if earnings disappoint further

Severe post-merger governance instability -- both the CEO and Chairman departed within weeks of completion, leaving the company run by interim leadership through a critical integration and cost-cutting phase, which raises real execution risk on the synergy targets

Expensive, long-dated sports rights commitments (AFL ~A$4.5bn over 7 years) are difficult to exit and have reportedly prompted attempts to renegotiate, signalling financial strain even as content costs remain largely fixed

No dividend currently being paid (interim dividend and DRP suspended) and ongoing one-off integration/restructuring charges continue to obscure underlying earnings power, making the stock hard to value with confidence until the merger fully beds down
